### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **62** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/sync-provenance-write.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-provenance-stamp.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**42** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b4f0b9832836e75a8300ece68acc970d1c7adf6`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/sync-provenance-write.ts`, `packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-provenance-stamp.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `environmentId (48 routes)`
- **21** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b4f0b9832836e75a8300ece68acc970d1c7adf6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0dd9b2d60ff17b4c406adbe53f01f6a9e4225011` — the merge of head `0f46c642ca89768b5124a5439c1119ae4ee5142f` into base `3b4f0b9832836e75a8300ece68acc970d1c7adf6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0dd9b2d60ff17b4c406adbe53f01f6a9e4225011 && git checkout 0dd9b2d60ff17b4c406adbe53f01f6a9e4225011
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3b4f0b9832836e75a8300ece68acc970d1c7adf6 0f46c642ca89768b5124a5439c1119ae4ee5142f && git checkout -B drift-repro 3b4f0b9832836e75a8300ece68acc970d1c7adf6 && git merge --no-ff 0f46c642ca89768b5124a5439c1119ae4ee5142f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b4f0b9832836e75a8300ece68acc970d1c7adf6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3b4f0b9832836e75a8300ece68acc970d1c7adf6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `167cb91793e160e32b009b99ea34120b94dc7932`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column-provenance.ts, packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-columns.ts, packages/spec/src/data/mapping.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.incremental-source-delete-policy-stated.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-delete-mark.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-window-read.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/pull-refusal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-provenance-stamp.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-run-ledger.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-sync-run.object.ts, packages/objectql/src/sync-provenance-write.ts, packages/runtime/src/job-handler-context.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/data.json, packages/spec/export-origins/data.json, packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json, packages/spec/liveness/object.json, packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/mapping.md, and as evidence packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-pull.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.integration.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull-undeclared-input-key.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/mapping-sync-in.test.ts, packages/spec/src/data/mapping-connector-source.test.ts

### ① Derived judgments

1. **New export `incrementalSourceDeleteRefusal` (`@objectstack/spec/data`): right.** A pure function of one source block that answers a sentence or `undefined`; additive; `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` carry it and nothing else moved. It is the one rule both doors ask (the `MappingSchema` refinement and both pulls), which is what keeps the parse and the run-time refusal from drifting. It sits beside `sourcedMappingModeRefusal` and is a parse rule, not runtime logic, so Prime Directive 2 holds.
2. **The parse-time refusal: right, and it is exactly ADR-0153 D3's ("An incremental source that cannot see deletes refuses at build").** The authored mappings that stop parsing, at path `[source, 'deletePolicy']`:
   - a mapping whose `connectorSource` declares a `watermark`, with `deletePolicy` absent or `'mark'` and no `deletedField`;
   - a mapping whose `datasourceSource` does not declare `full: true` (absent or `false`), with `deletePolicy` absent or `'mark'` and no `deletedField`.
   Nothing else stops parsing: `deletePolicy: 'ignore'` passes, a non-empty `deletedField` passes, a `connectorSource` with no `watermark` passes, a `datasourceSource` with `full: true` passes. The first shape is the released incremental connector binding (a `watermark` and no delete key, which is every incremental `connectorSource` written before the key existed), so the break reaches released metadata; the ADR decided it and measured no known producer.
3. **`sys_sync_run` gains `marked_deleted_count`, `deletes`, `skipped_null_watermark`: right.** Additive, optional, read-only columns on an engine-owned object; ADR-0153 D7 lists the marked-deleted and NULL-watermark counts and D3 names the `deletes` note. `deletes` is free text holding a closed set of seven notes (longest 28 characters against `maxLength: 64`); a `select` would state the set, which is a taste call.
4. **`deletePolicy` / `deletedField` liveness, both sources, `planned` to `live` with `authorWarn` and `authorHint` dropped: right.** Each row has a reader in the tree (`syncDeletePolicyOf`, `SyncDeleteMarker.afterBatch`, `markAbsent`), `paging` stays `planned`, and the count moves 24/9 to 28/5, which is the four rows. The flip lands with the reader, as the ADR's children table orders.
5. **Injected system columns: right, and no plan change.** The two spec files change one field description (`_sync_deleted_at`) and one doc comment; the plan, the column set and the index are untouched. The old text ("Not written yet") is false at this head, so the edit is owed here.
6. **Other surface the diff moves, each right:** the refusal reason `delete_policy_unhonourable` joins `ConnectorPullRefusalReason` (additive); `DatasourcePullResult.deletes` and `ConnectorSourcePullOutcome.deletes` are service-level additions the spec contract `ConnectorSourcePullResult` does not name (a caller through `IAutomationService` cannot read them typed; nothing needs them yet); `JobHandlerContext` gains optional `trigger` and `runId` (additive; `JobRunTrigger` already exists in `@objectstack/spec/contracts`).
7. **One run-time refusal the ADR does not name: a `synced` target with `systemFields: false` under `deletePolicy` absent or `'mark'` (`mapping_target_refused`).** The rule is sound (no row could carry the mark), but see S3: it is a second narrowing, judged only when the pull runs, and the ledger entry does not carry it.

### ② Semver level

- **Level: right.** `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` takes at least `minor` on every package the diff moves; the changeset bumps `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-automation` and `@objectstack/runtime` at `minor`. `@objectstack/objectql` moves by a doc comment only and is in the `fixed` group, so it needs no line.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: right.** Something an author could write is now refused, and nothing is widened on the declared arm (the new export, columns and context members are additive beside it).
- **`Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: right** (narrowed over added).
- **Breaking payload: carried.** The title carries `!`, the body carries the BREAKING banner, FROM (an incremental source under `deletePolicy` absent or `'mark'` with no `deletedField`) and TO (`deletedField: 'is_deleted'`, or `deletePolicy: 'ignore'`), and the one-line fix. The disposition is one marker, `registered incremental-source-delete-policy-stated`, and the id resolves to a file that is new in the diff.
- **Migration entry 18: right kind, right shape.** A `SemanticMigration` in `entries/semantic/`, file named `18.` plus the id as the README requires, no index touched, `registry.ts` not committed. A structured to-do rather than a D2 conversion is the correct call: a conversion that wrote `deletePolicy: 'ignore'` would restore the old behaviour, but ADR-0153 D3 makes the author state the choice, and an author who wrote `'mark'` meant marking. On a stored mapping: one without the keys is refused when it is pulled, with the parse's own sentence (`delete_policy_unhonourable`), and one with either key runs; the entry's `acceptanceCriteria` names only `os validate`, so a mapping stored at run time is reached by the pull's refusal alone (nit N8).
- **Gap: the second BREAKING bullet has no ledger row** (S3).

### ③ Boundary flags

Inputs read: card #32062 body and all 33 comments (claim 7145967588, release 7122297060, the slice orders and seat answers, every earlier report), PR #37179 body and file list, the net diff `49c8e0f0..167cb917` (27 files), ADR-0153 D3, D4, D7, the children table and the open points at `pr-37179`, ADR-0087 D2 and its 2026-08-13 addendum, the dev report 7150755927, and the 70 check-runs on the head (60 success, 10 skipped, 0 failure). Code outside the diff was read, not reviewed.

Dev flags and deviations (report 7150755927), each answered:

1. *Runtime package tests not run locally.* Answered: the runtime diff is two optional type members; `Test Core` (10 shards) and `TypeScript Type Check` are success on the head.
2. *Three derived gates NOT MEASURED locally.* Answered: `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` are success on the head.
3. *Dogfood battery, one timeout.* Answered with a reservation for the seat: the failing file (`approval-flow-name-per-namespace.dogfood.test.ts`) is not in the diff and passed alone. On the head the `Dogfood Regression Gate` check is success but its three shards are skipped, so the local run is the only dogfood reading at this head.
4. *Merge commit without the trailer pair; the Chinese reading section.* Process, not contract. Left to the seat.
5. *N4 of record 6791935060 not fixed (released CHANGELOG entries).* Accepted: a released entry is not a code PR's to edit. It still has no card ("noted, not filed"): escalated to the seat to file or carry.
6. *Reordered-`upsertKey` edge, stated and not fixed.* Accepted as stated (one wrong mark on one refused row for one run, cleared by the next write).
7. *Run-time tolerant readers (`syncDeletePolicyOf`, `incrementalSourceDeleteRefusal`).* Accepted as a second door for one rule; see N4 for the one lenient reading in it.
8. *Files outside the claim's surface.* The spec describe edits and the migration entry are consequences of D3 and of the narrowing; the objectql comment and `JobHandlerContext` are the carried nits. They are declared in the PR body only, while claim 7145967588 asks for them in the report (N9).
9. *ADR open point "two mappings on one target".* Not answered by the PR as the ADR asks: see S4.

SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5):

- **The "absent from source" set is computed in the database, and no source key set is held in memory: right.** `markAbsent` is one predicate on the target: `_sync_source` is this mapping, `_sync_deleted_at` is NULL, `_sync_pulled_at` is before the run's start, and on a datasource source the copied watermark is non-NULL and at or above `watermark.start`. The strict comparison is safe at the stored precision (`DATETIME(3)` on MySQL, finer elsewhere): a row written in the run's first millisecond compares equal and is left alone.
- **Refused keys are bounded** at 1001 in memory and 1000 in one `$nin`.
- **Marks are written one row at a time, after paging ids 500 at a time, although the engine has a single filtered `update` (`sync-run-ledger.ts` uses `multi: true`).** A reason is given in the module doc: the mark goes through the protocol's data door so the pull's write mark admits the `_sync_` column and hooks and audit run per row. Accepted. Cost stated for the seat: one round trip per marked row.
- **The built-in NULL-watermark count is the door's `COUNT`** (`limit: 1, count: true`), with a keyed paging fallback only when the door answers no total. Right.
- **`afterBatch` sends every key of the batch in one `$in`.** Bounded on a datasource source (1000 a page; at most the row cap, ceiling 10,000, on a floored window). Unbounded on a connector source: S1.

### ④ Design judgment

Against ADR-0153 D3, sentence by sentence, the tree holds on: mark and clear, never a physical delete; `ignore` as a no-op that also leaves earlier marks; the datasource completeness rule on both read paths; the range limit (copied watermark non-NULL and at or above `watermark.start`); the NULL-watermark count taken after the read, under the organization predicate, cap plus one through the floor; the connector rule (`paging` declared, `none` included; no `paging` records `unjudged, no paging declared`); the incremental refusal at both doors; a row marked earlier that reappears is cleared in `afterBatch`; an already-marked row keeps its first mark time; a target row of another mapping or of no mapping (`_sync_source` different or NULL) is never touched.

Break attempts that held: a full pull versus an incremental pull (an incremental run never calls `markAbsent`); a pull refused part-way (`readSourceInWindows` throws before the delete judgment, so no absence mark; `deletedField` marks already made on read rows stay, which is a positive reading and is right); `deletePolicy` unset, `'mark'`, `'ignore'`; a `deletedField` that is not a field of the datasource source (`source_binding_invalid`); two overlapping runs (each marks only rows stamped before its own start).

Break attempts that did not hold:

M1 (must-fix) — **a read row whose match key is blank is neither excluded nor counted, so a complete full pull marks rows the source still has.** `SyncDeleteMarker.afterBatch` returns early on a stamped row with no `_sync_external_id` (`sync-delete-mark.ts`, the `typeof key !== 'string'` line), before the `unwritten` bookkeeping. `stampSyncProvenance` stamps no key on a blank match key, and the runner refuses such a row (`BLANK_MATCH_KEY`, rewritten to a failed row by `refuseBlankMatchKeys`). So these rows are read, are not restamped, are not in the `$nin`, and do not move `canMarkAbsent`. Consequence: a source that stops sending the `upsertKey` field (the case #31810 measured; ADR-0153 D6's drift refusal has not landed) makes a full pull under `paging: { style: 'none' }`, or a `full: true` datasource pull whose key values went blank, refuse every row and then stamp `_sync_deleted_at` on every row of the mapping, one update and one automation run per row, with `deletes: judged`. This contradicts the contract the PR ships: the changeset ("a row the import runner refused was read, so it is not marked") and `jobs.mdx` ("one whose rows the import runner refused beyond a thousand, marks nothing by absence"). The pull cannot say which target rows a keyless record stands for, so it cannot judge absence at all. Fix: any read row the marker cannot name makes the run `unjudged, rows refused` (count it; one is enough), with a pin on each pull. The `unjudged, rows refused` arm has no test at this head on either pull (`git grep` finds the note only in source); pin the 1000-key limit in the same change.

S1 (should-fix) — **`afterBatch` on a connector source puts every key of the response in one `$in`.** The connector pull hands the whole response to one `afterBatch`; `toClear` (and `toMark`) are sent unchunked, and the SQL driver renders `$in` as one `whereIn` with one bound parameter per key. Once any row of the mapping carries a mark, a response past the dialect's parameter limit (32,766 on SQLite, 65,535 on Postgres) fails the pull after its rows were written, on every run. Chunk the two lists (the marker already pages at 500).

S2 (should-fix) — **`packages/spec/docs/SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md` (the `ordersPull` example at L470) teaches the shape this PR refuses.** Its "After" example, the migration target of the retired pipeline layer and the page `jobs.mdx` links for the watermark, is a `connectorSource` with a `watermark` and neither delete key. At this head it does not parse. Add `deletePolicy: 'ignore'` or a `deletedField` to the example in this PR.

S3 (should-fix) — **the second BREAKING change is in the changeset only.** A `synced` target with `systemFields: false` pulled under `deletePolicy` absent or `'mark'` was written before this PR and is refused after it. Entry 18's `surface` does not name it, so the upgrade guide and `migrate meta` say nothing of it, and it is judged only when the pull runs: `os validate` stays green while every scheduled run fails. `collectSourcedMappingErrors` has the objects at build and could refuse it there (Prime Directive 12). Add the prescription to the ledger (a second `registered` id, or this entry's surface) and file the build refusal for the spec lane.

S4 (should-fix) — **the ADR's open point is decided by the tree and denied by the PR.** ADR-0153 leaves "two mappings on one target object" to this child, "to be decided in its PR and said there". The tree decides it: each mapping marks only its own rows by `_sync_source`, nothing is refused. The PR body and the claim say the point stays open. Say the decision. Its residual needs a card: `_sync_source` holds the bare mapping name, while a mapping's identity is holder package plus name (record 6786503520 S1), so two packages' same-name mappings on one target mark and clear each other's rows run after run. The module doc names the case and not its consequence.

Nits, none blocking:

- N1 — a failure inside `stamp` loses the count: `marked` is added only after `stamp` returns, so a run that fails mid-mark closes with `marked_deleted_count` below the rows it stamped.
- N2 — `deletedField` truthiness is JavaScript's: a source that sends the text `'false'` or `'0'` has every row marked. On a connector source a misspelt `deletedField` reads as falsy on every record and marks nothing, silently. Say both in `jobs.mdx`, or judge the declared type on a datasource source.
- N3 — the floored NULL-watermark count reads whole rows up to the cap to count them; project the key.
- N4 — `syncDeletePolicyOf` reads a stored `deletePolicy` outside the enum as `'mark'`; the strict reading refuses it.
- N5 — the `connectorSource` liveness evidence names `pullConnectorSource`; the read is in `pullOnce`.
- N6 — `sys_sync_run.deletes` is also empty for a target that carries no provenance columns, while its description says "Empty when the pull failed".
- N7 — rows pulled before the provenance columns existed carry no `_sync_source`; one the source has since deleted is no mapping's row and is never marked. The changeset does not say so.
- N8 — entry 18's `acceptanceCriteria` names `os validate` only; a mapping stored at run time learns of the rule from the failed pull.
- N9 — the report's `deviations` omit the files outside the claim's surface that the PR body lists.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-32062-sync-in-d3-deletes`
Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzgv2LZN1W2qSYTZvYs`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 席位核对 — REWORK · repo:objectstack#3 · head 167cb917 · 2026-11-25T02:41Z

L1: REWORK (L1-w, zone wf-A)
Head-sha: `167cb91793e160e32b009b99ea34120b94dc7932`

The L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on this head is **FAIL**: comment 7151034259, claim 7150802612. I adopt its M1 and S1–S4 as they stand. I checked M1 against the tree: in `SyncDeleteMarker.afterBatch`, a stamped row with no string `_sync_external_id` returns before the refused-key bookkeeping, so it is neither excluded nor counted. If every row of a complete full pull is keyless and refused, `markAbsent` then marks the mapping's every row with `deletes: judged`. **Tier H** by card size: six PRs, 7,804 changed lines on #32062. After a final ACCEPT plus an L2 PASS it goes to the seat for the approver. Never ready, queue or arm it here.

### Must-fix (L1)

- **L1 M1. The changeset does not name `@objectstack/objectql`.** `packages/objectql/src/sync-provenance-write.ts` moves (the N8 sentence in `refuseHookSyncProvenanceWrite`'s docblock), and `@objectstack/objectql` is published. `l1-face`: "published package(s) touched with no changeset entry … @objectstack/objectql". Add `'@objectstack/objectql': patch`. The criterion is "a published package touched", not the size of the change.

### Should-fix (L1)

- **L1 S1. The claim's file surface was not amended for the files outside it.** The PR body's acceptance notes list them with reasons: `packages/objectql/src/sync-provenance-write.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/job-handler-context.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/injected-system-column*.ts`, the spec migration entry and generated artefacts. The claim (7145967588) still names only service-automation, `mapping.zod.ts` plus liveness rows, `sys_sync_run`, the docs and changesets. The zone amends the claim in the same round. The PR body already carries the evidence. (The L2's N9, the report's `deviations` omitting them, is the same gap.)

### Must-fix and should-fix (from the L2, adopted; details in 7151034259)

- **L2 M1.** A keyless read row slips the refused-row guard, and a pull whose rows all lack the key marks every row. Make any keyless read row mean `unjudged, rows refused`, with a pin on both pulls. The `unjudged, rows refused` arm also has no test yet.
- **L2 S1.** On a connector source, `afterBatch` sends the whole response's keys in one `$in`. Chunk them below the dialect's bound-parameter limit.
- **L2 S2.** The `ordersPull` example in `packages/spec/docs/SYNC_ARCHITECTURE.md` (around L470, linked from `jobs.mdx`) is now refused at parse. Fix it.
- **L2 S3.** The second BREAKING arm (`systemFields: false` under `'mark'`) is judged at run time only and is not named by migration entry 18. Name it in entry 18, and either refuse it at parse too or say plainly that `os validate` will not catch it.
- **L2 S4.** The tree decides ADR-0153's "two mappings on one target" open point (each marks only its own `_sync_source`, no refusal), but the PR body says it stays open. State the decision in the PR body and the ADR note the open point asks for. File the bare-name residual as a card: two packages' same-name mappings share a `_sync_source`.

Nits N1–N9 are listed in the L2 record. Fix any that ride the same push; the rest each need a follow-up card under the nit rule.

### Read and found right (head 167cb917)

- `l1-face --pr 37179`: 11 of 13 items clean. `changeset` is flagged (L1 M1 above). `dogfood` is flagged as owed, read below. The draft is against `main`, and `Part of #32062` binds no closing keyword. The declarations are `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` · `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` · `Skills-docs: none` with its grep and control. Floors and all checks are green: 60 success, 10 expected skips, 0 failed. `mergeable_state` clean.
